title: JavaScript Reference
description: A compact reference of the JavaScript syntax, built-in methods and browser APIs covered in the tutorial, grouped by topic, with syntax, a short example and the lesson that explains each one.

entries.name: let
entries.summary: Declares a block-scoped variable whose value can be reassigned later.

example.code:
let count = 0;
count = count + 1;

notes: Use let only when the value must change; prefer const otherwise.
Cannot be used before its declaration line (temporal dead zone).

entries.name: const
entries.summary: Declares a block-scoped binding that cannot be reassigned. The object or array it holds can still be modified.

entries.name: typeof
entries.summary: Returns the type of a value as a string: "string", "number", "boolean", "undefined", "object", "function", "bigint" or "symbol".

example.code:
typeof 42;        // "number"
typeof null;      // "object" (historical quirk)
typeof [];        // "object"; use Array.isArray

entries.name: console.log()
entries.summary: Prints one or more values to the developer tools console, separated by spaces. console.warn and console.error do the same with a highlight.

example.code: console.log("Total:", 42);   // Total: 42

entries.name: Template literal
entries.summary: A string in backticks that can span lines and embed expressions with ${...}.

example.code:
const name = "Ada";
const msg = `Hello, ${name}! You have ${2 + 3} new messages.`;

entries.name: === and !==
entries.summary: Strict equality compares type and value with no conversion. Prefer it over == and !=, which convert types first.

example.code:
5 === "5";   // false
5 == "5";    // true (converted)

entries.name: Conditional (ternary) operator
entries.summary: An expression that picks one of two values depending on a condition.

example.code: const label = count === 1 ? "item" : "items";

notes: Keep it to a single level; nested ternaries are hard to read.

entries.name: if / else if / else
entries.summary: Runs the first block whose condition is truthy; else runs when none matched.
notes: Falsy values: false, 0 (and -0, 0n), "", null, undefined, NaN. Everything else is truthy.

entries.name: switch
entries.summary: Compares one value against several cases with strict equality; execution falls through to the next case unless break is used.

entries.name: for
entries.summary: A counting loop with an initialiser, a condition checked before each pass and an update after each pass.
notes: continue skips to the next pass; break leaves the loop.

entries.name: for...of
entries.summary: Loops over the elements of an array, the characters of a string or any iterable such as Map and Set.

entries.name: for...in
entries.summary: Loops over the property names of an object. Not intended for arrays; use for...of there.

entries.name: while / do...while
entries.summary: Repeats while the condition is truthy. do...while runs the body once before checking.
notes: Make sure something inside the body moves the condition towards false, or the loop never ends.

entries.name: function declaration
entries.summary: Defines a named, reusable block of code with parameters and an optional return value. Declarations are hoisted.
notes: A function without return (or with a bare return) returns undefined.

entries.name: Arrow function
entries.summary: A compact function expression. A single-expression body returns implicitly, and this is taken from the surrounding scope.

example.code:
const square = (n) => n * n;
const makeUser = (name) => ({ name });   // parentheses return an object

notes: Do not use arrows as object methods that need their own this.

entries.name: Default parameters
entries.summary: Gives a parameter a value to use when the argument is missing or undefined.

entries.name: Rest parameters
entries.summary: Collects any number of trailing arguments into an array.

entries.name: Closure
entries.summary: A function that keeps access to the variables of the scope where it was created, even after that scope has finished.
notes: Used for private state, callbacks and function factories.

entries.name: push / pop / shift / unshift
entries.summary: Add or remove elements at the end (push, pop) or the start (unshift, shift). All four mutate the array.

entries.name: map()
entries.summary: Returns a new array with the result of calling a function on every element.

entries.name: filter()
entries.summary: Returns a new array containing only the elements for which the function returns a truthy value.

entries.name: reduce()
entries.summary: Combines all elements into one value by calling a function with an accumulator and each element; the second argument is the starting value.

entries.name: find() / findIndex() / includes()
entries.summary: find returns the first element matching a test (or undefined), findIndex its position (or -1), includes checks for a value with strict equality.
notes: some and every return a boolean for 'at least one' and 'all'.

entries.name: slice() / splice()
entries.summary: slice copies a range without changing the array; splice removes or inserts elements in place.

entries.name: sort() / toSorted()
entries.summary: Sorts elements; without a compare function they are compared as strings. sort mutates, toSorted (ES2023) returns a sorted copy.
notes: toReversed and with are the non-mutating companions of reverse and index assignment.

entries.name: Object literal
entries.summary: Creates an object from key: value pairs. Read properties with dot notation or brackets when the key is dynamic.

example.code:
const book = { title: "JS", pages: 300 };
book.title;        // "JS"
book["pages"];     // 300
book.year = 2024;  // add

entries.name: Object.keys() / values() / entries()
entries.summary: Return arrays of an object's property names, values or [key, value] pairs.

entries.name: ?. optional chaining
entries.summary: Reads a property or calls a method only if the left side is not null or undefined; otherwise the expression is undefined.

example.code: order.customer?.address?.city;   // undefined instead of a TypeError

entries.name: ?? nullish coalescing
entries.summary: Returns the right side only when the left side is null or undefined. Unlike ||, it keeps 0, "" and false.

example.code: const retries = config.retries ?? 3;   // keeps an explicit 0

entries.name: ... spread
entries.summary: Expands an array or object into a new literal or into function arguments. Produces a shallow copy.

example.code:
const settings = { ...defaults, fontSize: 18 };
Math.max(...[3, 11, 7]);   // 11

notes: Use structuredClone(value) for a deep copy.

entries.name: Destructuring
entries.summary: Unpacks array elements or object properties into variables, with optional defaults and renaming.
entries.syntax: const [a, b] = arr;   const { x, y: alias = 0 } = obj;

entries.name: JSON.parse() / JSON.stringify()
entries.summary: Convert between JSON text and JavaScript values. parse throws a SyntaxError on invalid JSON; stringify can indent with a third argument.

example.code:
const user = JSON.parse('{"name":"Ada"}');
JSON.stringify({ a: 1 });   // '{"a":1}'

notes: undefined, functions and symbols are dropped; dates become strings.

entries.name: length, at(), slice()
entries.summary: length counts characters, at(i) reads one (negative counts from the end), slice(start, end) extracts a range. Strings are immutable: every method returns a new string.

example.code:
"JavaScript".slice(0, 4);   // "Java"
"JavaScript".at(-1);        // "t"

entries.name: split() / join()
entries.summary: split breaks a string into an array at a separator; join combines array elements into a string.

entries.name: includes() / startsWith() / indexOf()
entries.summary: Search inside a string: includes and startsWith/endsWith return booleans, indexOf returns the position or -1. All are case-sensitive.

example.code:
"hello world".includes("world");   // true
"hello".indexOf("z");              // -1

entries.name: replace() / replaceAll()
entries.summary: replace changes the first match of a string pattern; replaceAll changes every match.

entries.name: trim() / padStart() / toUpperCase()
entries.summary: trim removes surrounding whitespace, padStart pads to a length with a character, toUpperCase and toLowerCase change case.

entries.name: Number() / parseInt() / toFixed()
entries.summary: Number converts a whole string (NaN if invalid), parseInt and parseFloat read the leading number, toFixed formats with a fixed number of decimals and returns a string.
notes: Test for NaN with Number.isNaN(value), not with ===.

entries.name: Math.round() / floor() / ceil() / random()
entries.summary: Rounding helpers plus max, min, abs, sqrt and random, which returns a decimal from 0 up to (not including) 1.

example.code:
Math.round(4.5);                      // 5
Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1;    // 1 to 6

entries.name: querySelector() / querySelectorAll()
entries.summary: Find the first element matching a CSS selector (or null), or a NodeList of every match. getElementById("id") is a fast alternative for ids.

example.code:
const title = document.querySelector("#title");
const items = document.querySelectorAll(".item");

notes: A NodeList has forEach but not map; use Array.from or spread first.

entries.name: textContent / innerHTML
entries.summary: textContent reads or sets the text of an element literally; innerHTML parses markup. Use textContent for user-provided or server-provided text.

example.code:
title.textContent = "Hello"; box.innerHTML = "

Own markup only

";

entries.name: classList
entries.summary: Adds, removes, toggles and tests CSS classes without manipulating the class string.

example.code:
button.classList.toggle("active");
if (panel.classList.contains("open")) { /* ... */ }

entries.name: createElement() / append() / remove()
entries.summary: Create a detached element, fill it, insert it with append, prepend, before or after, and delete it with remove.

entries.name: addEventListener()
entries.summary: Registers a function to run when an event of the given type happens on the element. Pass the function itself, not a call.
notes: Events bubble: a listener on a parent sees events from its children (event delegation).
removeEventListener needs the same function reference.

entries.name: event.preventDefault()
entries.summary: Cancels the browser's built-in action for the event, such as submitting a form or following a link.

entries.name: Promise
entries.summary: Represents a value that will be available later. Consume it with then, catch and finally; combine several with Promise.all or allSettled.

example.code:
const wait = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
wait(100).then(() => console.log("done"));

notes: Promise.all rejects on the first failure; Promise.allSettled reports every outcome.

entries.name: async / await
entries.summary: An async function returns a promise; inside it, await pauses until a promise settles and throws on rejection, so try/catch works.
entries.syntax: async function f() { const v = await promise; }
notes: Forgetting await gives you the promise instead of the value.

entries.name: fetch()
entries.summary: Sends an HTTP request and resolves to a Response. Check response.ok, then read the body with response.json() or response.text().
notes: fetch only rejects on network failure, not on 404 or 500 responses.
POST JSON with method, a Content-Type header and a JSON.stringify body.

entries.name: setTimeout() / setInterval()
entries.summary: Run a function once after a delay, or repeatedly at an interval, in milliseconds. Both return an id for clearTimeout / clearInterval.

example.code:
const id = setInterval(() => console.log("tick"), 1000);
setTimeout(() => clearInterval(id), 5000);

entries.name: try / catch / finally / throw
entries.summary: try wraps code that may fail, catch receives the error, finally always runs. throw raises an Error object of your own.
notes: Extend Error for custom types; pass { cause } to keep the original error.

entries.name: import / export
entries.summary: Share values between ES modules. Named exports are imported in braces; the single default export is imported without them.
entries.syntax: export const x = 1;   export default fn;   import fn, { x } from "./m.js";
notes: Load with <script type="module">; module scripts are deferred and strict.
import() with parentheses loads a module on demand.

entries.name: class
entries.summary: A template for objects with a constructor, methods, getters, static members, private #fields and inheritance through extends and super.
entries.syntax: class Name extends Parent { constructor() { super(); } method() {} }
notes: Instances are created with new; calling a class without it throws a TypeError.
